Definition: from the same as G154; a cause (as if asked for), i.e. (logical) reason (motive, matter), (legal) crime (alleged or proved):--accusation, case, cause, crime, fault, (wh-)ere(-fore).
BiblicalUsage: The word is a cause, a reason, or a formal charge. Over Jesus' head the soldiers nail His accusation — THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS — and Pilate keeps saying he finds no fault in him, no cause for death. Paul, years later, tells the Roman Jews he was delivered prisoner though I have committed nothing against the people. The word keeps appearing wherever men must say why someone stands accused.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the irony is the sermon. The only charge Rome could pin on Jesus was His kingship, and Pilate's no fault is the verdict of history: the innocent Man died under a true accusation — He is the King — and a false crime.
